title: Extract each have of a proof sketch into a standalone theorem (HILBERT subgoal-extraction prompt)
intent: Turn a proof sketch — the main theorem with its `have` statements left as `sorry` — into one standalone theorem per hole, keeping the `have` name and the context of the preceding subgoals, so each hole can be filled by a separate prover and the sketch's own application lines remain untouched.

children.name: name-preserved
children.statement: Each extracted theorem keeps the `have` statement's name (instruction 1).
children.closed_by: instruction 1 ('Use the same name as the have statements for the theorems'); the name is what lets the sketch's application lines stay untouched and what the completeness check matches against

children.name: context-carried
children.statement: Each theorem carries the relevant context of the preceding subgoals, with preceding theorems presented as hypotheses unchanged (instructions 2 and 8).

children.name: one-per-hole
children.statement: There are as many extracted theorems as `sorry`s in the sketch (instruction 3).
children.closed_by: instruction 3; enforced by `_check_and_extract_missing_subgoals`, which re-prompts until `extract_all_have_names(original_sketch)` is covered and abandons the attempt otherwise

children.name: statement-only
children.statement: Each theorem is a bare statement with a `sorry` proof and no imports, open statements or definitions (instructions 4-6).

children.name: conclusion-stable
children.statement: The conclusion of each extracted theorem and the premise names/types are kept exactly as in the subgoal (instructions 7 and 10).

applicability.goal_shape: A Lean 4 proof sketch: a main theorem whose `by` block is a sequence of named `have` statements (each proved by `sorry`) applied to prove the goal, with no concrete lemma names until the extraction runs.
applicability.use_when: you have a skeleton proof with `sorry`-ed `have` holes to farm out to per-hole provers, and you want each hole to become a self-contained theorem that keeps the `have` name so the sketch's application lines do not change.
applicability.avoid_when: the sketch has no named `have` statements (the handler returns early, `_check_and_extract_missing_subgoals` returning `True, []`); a hole needs its conclusion changed or its statement strengthened or weakened (instructions 7-8 forbid it); or the holes share context that cannot be lifted into clean standalone statements. The prompt only extracts: it does not check that the extracted statements are true or sufficient, which must be done downstream.

claims.claim: The prompt maps each `sorry` hole to exactly one theorem and keeps the `have` name: instruction 1 reads 'Use the same name as the have statements for the theorems' and instruction 3 reads 'There should be as many extracted theorems as `sorry`s in the given theorem'.

The handler refuses to proceed unless every `have` of the sketch was extracted: `_check_and_extract_missing_subgoals` computes `all_have_names = extract_all_have_names(original_sketch)` and `missing_names = [name for name in all_have_names if name not in extracted_names]`, and `extract_subgoals_from_sketch` returns `[]` — abandoning the attempt — when that check fails.

After extraction each child is renamed under the parent theorem name — `new_name = f"{current_name}_{parent_theorem_name}"` (line 2000) — so `h0` under `main_theorem` becomes `h0_main_theorem`; the rename is called from the orchestration loop at line 2050.

The prompt carries a standing constraint against undefined natural-number arithmetic in the extracted statements: 'Do NOT, under ANY circumstances, allow division and subtraction operations on natural number literals with UNDEFINED types, unless REQUIRED by the theorem statement.'

The extraction prompt is a single 24-line string (lines 64-87) with 10 numbered instructions (lines 65-75) and two 'IMPORTANT INSTRUCTION' paragraphs (lines 77 and 79); the consuming method `extract_subgoals_from_sketch` spans 67 lines (1432-1498).
claims.evidence: read of the copied files src/prompts/hilbert.py and src/models/HILBERTWorker.py

metrics.how_counted: instructions counted as the numbered items on lines 66-75 of hilbert.py; the two IMPORTANT INSTRUCTION paragraphs start on lines 77 and 79; the prompt string spans lines 64-87; the handler method extract_subgoals_from_sketch spans lines 1432-1498

consequences: The lift creates one standalone theorem per `sorry`-ed `have`, with the `have` name preserved and the sketch's application lines untouched, so the sketch stays valid once each child is proved. Obligations it creates: (i) name and conclusion fidelity (instructions 1, 7, 10) — a child that changes its conclusion or argument types would break the sketch, and the prompt forbids repairing a hole by strengthening or weakening its statement during extraction; (ii) coverage (instruction 3) — the handler re-prompts for missing `have` names and abandons the attempt if they cannot be covered; (iii) statement hygiene — the two IMPORTANT INSTRUCTION paragraphs filter ill-typed natural-number arithmetic, but this is a literal model instruction, not a type check, so it can be misapplied. What the prompt does not check is truth and sufficiency: whether each extracted theorem is true and whether the assembled sketch closes is decided downstream (the assembly prompt USE_SKETCH_AND_THEOREMS_TO_PROVE, whose instruction is 'ALWAYS use the supplied theorems', and the no-`sorry` check `_check_for_sorries` on the completed proof). Failure modes: an unnamed `have` (e.g. `have : P := ...`) yields an empty name in `extract_all_have_names` and is silently dropped from the completeness comparison; the coverage check is by name only, so two distinct holes with the same `have` name would count as one.
